text: If F1, F2 and F3 are propositional formulae such that F1∧F2→F3 and F1∧F2→~F3 are both tautologies, then which of the following is true:
options: Both F1 and F2 are tautologies
The conjunction F1∧F2 is not satisfiable
answer: Option (B) - the conjunction F1∧F2 is not satisfiable
solution: F1∧F2→F3 and F1∧F2→~F3 are both tautologies. Taking contrapositives gives ~F3→~(F1∧F2) and F3→~(F1∧F2); resolving these on F3 yields ~(F1∧F2), i.e. F1∧F2 is a contradiction and hence unsatisfiable. Note F1,F2,F3 are formulae, not propositional variables.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page - GATE CSE 1991 Q.3(xii) with community solutions (accepted answer by Deepak Poonia)
answer_evidence: So, for this GATE 1991 question, the answer will be Option B But the method of some students is Not correct.
